bug_semantics: Akaunting's common BulkActions dispatcher takes a request-controlled handle and invokes it as a method on the resolved BulkAction class (for example App\BulkActions\Auth\Users). Authorization is supposed to come from the $actions metadata, but the 3.1.21 dispatcher only consults $actions[$handle]['permission'] when the submitted handle is a direct array key. That misses (1) modal submit handles such as update, declared under edit via 'handle' => 'update', and (2) callable methods such as destroy that exist on the class/base but are not action keys (delete is the keyed alias). An authenticated user with only read-admin-panel (default Manager) can POST /{company_id}/common/bulk-actions/auth/users with handle=update&roles[]=<admin> or handle=destroy and escalate or delete users, because UpdateUser/DeleteUser do not re-check update-auth-users/delete-auth-users.
flaw_origin: The first public write of this mechanism is 6d50fa844252a4d2325d7ad0362db5389fefc52b (2019-11-16, 'v2 first commit'). That commit created app/Http/Controllers/Common/BulkActions.php with unconstrained $bulk_actions->{$request->get('handle')}($request) (line 32), registered POST bulk-actions/{group}/{type}, and added Auth\Users with permissioned enable/disable/delete keys plus a non-keyed destroy() that delete() simply forwards to. Parent 5b23e9c2c4b2f00ba2606df88731d6e63fc1d814 (v1.3.17) has no BulkActions tree. No finer public v2 members exist to decompose the rewrite landing. 2000de7b later added the direct-key-only permission isset, which is the CWE-863 shape in 3.1.21 but did not first write the dispatch; d9c07645/f15f8c68 only refactored the same call and added the update modal gadget.

reasoning: CVE-2026-19198 / GHSA-v47h-4p48-9r9r is a real CWE-863 in Akaunting 3.1.21: BulkActions::action() treats the request handle as a method name and only enforces $actions[$handle]['permission'] when that handle is a direct key, so handle=update and handle=destroy on Auth\Users bypass update-auth-users/delete-auth-users for any admin-panel user. CVE.org is PUBLISHED; this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The smallest first write of the vulnerable mechanism is 6d50fa844252a4d2325d7ad0362db5389fefc52b, which introduced unconstrained request-handle dispatch plus the Users destroy() gadget that is not an $actions key. Immediate parent 5b23e9c2c4b2f00ba2606df88731d6e63fc1d814 is present and has no BulkActions files, so introducer_parent_absent=false. The 3146-file 'v2 first commit' is a rewrite landing, but it is the smallest surviving public object and cannot be decomposed. Later 2000de7b is a partial permission patch that created the 3.1.21 CWE-863 shape without introducing dispatch; 3.0/3.1 commits are refactors or gadget additions, not BICs. Direct fix 96c38008cf6f907e3e7341d9660de2912e0f2f13 allowlists handles and is in 3.2.0/3.2.1, after 3.1.21. BIC commit-object author/committer/trailers have no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
